sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Adansonia digitata is a deciduous African baobab usually 20–25 m tall, with a massive trunk. Its leaves are typically divided into five to seven leaflets; large white flowers hang from the branches, and the woody fruit contains seeds in a dry, floury pulp. It occurs in tropical dry woodland and savanna.

sections.title: Food uses and related baobabs
sections.text: The fruit pulp, leaves and seeds are used as foods in documented African food systems. Use varies by region and preparation. This widespread African species differs from A. perrieri and A. suarezensis, which are Madagascan baobabs with restricted ranges and separate conservation assessments.
